# 300.00 USD charged to a US dollar card at 1.35, then 500.00 USD paid onto it
# — 250.00 from B and 250.00 from C, each giving its own cost basis.
#
# 300.00 repays the card and 200.00 moves to its credit, but nothing in the
# transaction says whether the 200.00 that only moved came out of B's cost
# basis or C's, and which one decides what each is left holding. Drawn down in
# full, both would fall by 250.00 and the held side's cost bases would stand
# for 200.00 fewer dollars than its accounts hold. So it is refused, and the
# refusal asks for the 200.00 moved as a transaction of its own.
#
# Imported into the book usd_moved_out_of_an_empty_account.txt makes.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_balance_past_zero_has_a_cost_basis_on_the_other_side.py.
2034-01-20 * "Travel charged to the card"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Travel 405.00 CAD
	Liabilities:USD Card -300.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "27/20"
		value: "-405.00"
		guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000008"

2034-02-01 * "Pay 500.00 USD onto the card from B and C"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD B -250.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "27/20"
		value: "-337.50"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000002"
	Assets:USD C -250.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-325.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000003"
	Liabilities:USD Card 500.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1333/1000"
		value: "666.50"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000008"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
